answer: Clone farms fail a one-gauge weir. A key stakes 1.47 POA at a ridge gauge and posts a 24-byte silt hash. A prism fans the hash into three bands held by separate notaries. Over 14 hours it sends seven river receipts, each an 18-byte slip signed 52 minutes apart from a fresh /18; each notary countersigns only its band within 8 minutes. Auditors void a reused /15 or two receipts closer than 44 minutes. If four gauges open under one wallet in 8 hours, or two silt hashes share two bands, all bands void and the stake stays locked. A late countersign leaves that band dark; no second gauge is cut.
